C0.quote: a method of detecting gerrymandering that can be applied to such
C0.note: The paper studies districting manipulation of FPTP elections, a strategic aspect of a voting procedure. Its main object is a statistical detection method, which makes eligibility borderline.

C1.quote: development of a nonparametric methods for detecting gerrymandering
C1.note: OT: proposal of a statistical detection methodology, which the paper calls its main contribution. SI: Monte Carlo observation and tests on simulated districting plans. EM: application to real election datasets.

C3.1.note: Voter strategic behaviour is not analysed.

C5.1.note: The evaluation criterion is statistical deviation of party seat shares from an estimated seats-votes function, not welfare, voter representation or proportionality. This is borderline, since partisan bias concerns parties' representation.

C0.reason: The paper defines gerrymandering as manipulation of district boundaries in FPTP elections and simulates seat-maximising districting plans, so it studies a strategic aspect of a voting procedure, the kind of districting the codebook's DIS stakeholder type covers.

C1.reason: The paper presents its main contribution as a methodological proposal (OT); the simulation and empirical tests are secondary validations, so OT is the primary type.

C6.DIS.reason: The seat-maximising ILP is a tool for generating test plans, not a modelled agent taking actions in the paper's formal model.

C6.VOT.reason: Voters cast votes that enter the model as fixed, exogenous data, which counts as a present non-strategic type.

C7.1.reason: Only one type (VOT) is present, so the item is NA; B's note that no types are present is inaccurate.

C8.1.reason: With the district designer not present, no type is strategic, so C8 does not apply.

C9.1.reason: The introduction claims what the results mean for real-world decisions, namely identifying elections that need further investigation.

C9.2.reason: The assumptions needed for the usefulness claim are stated explicitly in Section 1.3.
